title: Void/Decline buttons visible to any user â€” comment says 'Admin only' but no role check wraps them
detail: Line 182-188 renders the Void and Decline action buttons for every non-terminal contract. The inline comment says 'Void / Decline - Admin only, non-terminal', and line 28 destructures `isAdmin, isManager` from usePortalUser â€” but neither variable is ever checked before rendering the buttons. Line 9 imports RoleGuard but never uses it. Any authenticated user currently sees and can click Void/Decline on any contract, triggering a forward-only, audit-logged state change. For external-customer user testing this is a real data-integrity risk: a customer clicks through the tool and nukes a live contract.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:28 `const { isAdmin, isManager, userEmail } = usePortalUser();` â€” isAdmin/isManager imported but unused. Line 182-188 btn-void and btn-decline rendered without a guard. Line 9 `import RoleGuard from '../RoleGuard.jsx';` â€” imported but never referenced elsewhere in the file.
recommendedFix: Wrap the void/decline block in `{isAdmin() && !isTerminal && (...)}` (note the `()` â€” isAdmin is a function per usePortalUser.jsx:112). Same pattern as CustomerDetail ProgramsTab line 506. Alternative: use the imported RoleGuard with `require="admin"`. Remove the unused RoleGuard import if not used.

title: reload() contract GET lists `dcfg_contract_number` twice in the $select clause
detail: Line 48: the $select contains `,dcfg_contract_number,...,dcfg_contract_number,...` â€” the column is repeated. Dataverse tolerates duplicate $select entries, so the call succeeds, but it signals the clause was edited by concatenation without review. No runtime impact, but worth cleaning up.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:48 apiGet URL â€” grep reveals two occurrences of dcfg_contract_number in the same comma-separated list.
recommendedFix: Delete the second `dcfg_contract_number,` from the $select list in line 48.

title: reload() error routes to top-level error banner instead of toast â€” replaces entire page content
detail:
Line 60: `reload().catch(e => setError(e.message)).finally(...)`. setError then causes the whole page to render `
{error}
` at line 141 â€” replacing the contract detail UI with a raw error string. Any transient error (network blip, 429 throttle) kills the whole screen instead of showing a dismissible toast. Also, commitTransition at line 101 uses the same pattern â€” a failed status-change sets the page-level error and nukes the current view.
evidence: ContractDetail.jsx:60 initial load, 101 commitTransition setError, 141 render `{error}` full-page.
recommendedFix: Split into two error paths: hard load failure (initial contract fetch returns null) keeps the full-page banner for clarity. Transient errors from commitTransition and later operations should use a toast (`const toast = useToast()` â€” already imported via Toast component elsewhere) so the user sees the failure without losing the screen.
